lab_table.hypothesis: Small-paste-scale hypothesis: misses concentrate in the low size tertile, so shrinking pastes to the missed size range (inclusion 0.3-0.7x, patches/scratches 0.4-0.8x) should raise small-instance recall. Confirmed if mAP50 beats the balanced/default control, especially inclusion AP50 and low-tertile recall, without a precision collapse.

Allocation hypothesis: inclusion is the starved, worst class (10 real images, AP50 0.179, 148 missed), so at the default scale range, shifting 30 of 50 images to inclusion should lift inclusion AP50 most. Confirmed if inclusion AP50 rises substantially and overall mAP50 beats the balanced control; if not, allocation balance matters less than scale.

Combination hypothesis: if small scale and inclusion-heavy allocation both help, their combination should be the round's best (additive effects). Confirmed if it has the highest mAP50; if it underperforms A or B, the two factors interact negatively and I should not stack them in later rounds.
CONTROL (added by the lab): default generation recipe, balanced allocation.

lesson: Shrinking pastes (0.3-0.8x) is a net loss: it helped inclusion/patches but collapsed scratches AP50 (-0.126), so do NOT shrink scratches. Inclusion-heavy allocation (30/10/10) at the default 0.6-1.4 scale was the round's best (0.5746, inclusion 0.329). Next: keep default scale for scratches, try small scale ONLY for inclusion/patches, and probe whether the small scratches cost from inclusion-heavy allocation can be recovered (e.g. slightly more scratches or any_class backgrounds).
